answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because thread only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, lantern is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any glacier approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
